questions.question: Surface area of a sphere with radius r =
questions.explanation: Surface area of sphere = 4πr². Volume = (4/3)πr³. Hemisphere: curved surface = 2πr², total surface = 3πr² (curved + circular base). The sphere has no edges or vertices.

If the radius of a sphere is doubled, surface area becomes:
questions.explanation: SA = 4πr². New r = 2r. New SA = 4π(2r)² = 4π×4r² = 16πr² = 4×SA. Surface area is 4 times (scales as r²). Compare: volume scales as r³ — so doubling radius gives 8× volume but only 4× surface area.

A spherical balloon is inflated from r = 7 cm to r = 14 cm. By what factor does the volume increase?
questions.explanation: V ∝ r³. V₁ = (4/3)π×7³ = (4/3)π×343. V₂ = (4/3)π×14³ = (4/3)π×2744. Ratio = 2744/343 = 8. Volume increases 8 times. (Doubling radius → 2³ = 8 times volume. This is why a small increase in radius causes a big change in volume.)

Formula summary — for the same radius r:
Surface area of sphere : Total SA of hemisphere : Curved SA of hemisphere =
questions.explanation: Sphere SA = 4πr². Hemisphere TSA = curved + base = 2πr² + πr² = 3πr². Hemisphere CSA = 2πr². Ratio: 4πr² : 3πr² : 2πr² = 4 : 3 : 2. Useful to remember: hemisphere TSA is ¾ of sphere SA; hemisphere CSA is ½ of sphere SA.
